newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt ends up, Ecuador Bradys retain gains.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt ends up, Ecuador Bradys retain gains.

text.p: Emerging debt prices ended Monday's trading session higher across the board with Ecuador Bradys stealing the spotlight posting gains of as much as three points on the day, traders said.

Ecuador wound down the New York trading session off its earlier highs but retained substantial gains. PDI bonds ECPDI=RR ended up 2-3/8 points to trade at a 60-3/4 bid. News that the government had appointed interim president Rosalia Arteaga over the weekend, following President Abdela Bucaram's decision to finally step down from office, triggered the rally, traders said.

The measure was aimed at ending the crisis that erupted last Thursday when President Abdala Bucaram was ousted by Congress on the grounds of "mental incompetence" but refused to step down until Sunday.
Last week PDI bonds had been trading at a 66 bid but tumbled to a low of 58 bid by Friday during the crisis.

"You'll see some improvement in the market today but going forward I suspect its probably a short-term rally as the complexities of the situation become more apparent you'll probably see a risk premium begin to reemerge," said emerging market analyst, Brian Barish.

"I don't think there's a constitutional mechanism in Ecuador for dealing with a situation where the president of the country becomes somewhat irrational," Barish said. "How do you define a constitutional mechanism for succession under those circumstances.
Meanwhile, on Tuesday, congress is expected to pass legislation allowing it to reappoint its leader, Fabian Alarcon, as president, while Arteaga assumes her original role as vice president.
Alarcon would serve as interim head of state until August 10, 1998, then hand over power to a new president chosen in general elections to be held in May or June next year.
Still, analysts said a more permanent solution is needed.

"The market's taking this surprisingly optimistically, but the governmental situation is still in a holding pattern and while this is a good interim solution, we still don't know what it means longer-term," said Richard Segal, head of fixed income research at Santander investments.

"A key issue for the financial markets is whether the Eurobond that was mandated not too long goes through, Segal added."The Eurobond is required to pay back some bridge financing and if the financing doesn't come through they're going to need to repay it somehow."
"If they've already used the money they've raised it could be quite difficult," he added.
Turning to other Brady debt prices, Peru Citi bonds PEFLG91=RR were up 5/8 while Peru PDIs PEPDI=RR were unchanged.

On Tuesday, hostage talks are scheduled to resume between Peru's government and The Tupac Amaru Reveloutionary Movement rebels who continues to hold 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Rebels continue to demand the release of 400 jailed comrades.

Among other debt issues, Argentina par bonds AR4C23=RR ended the day up 3/8, Brazil Par bonds BR4024=RR were up 1/8 at 66-3/8 and Russian Vnesh US$ bonds RUVNUSLNS=RR ended the trading day up 1/2 at 82 bid.
